article.title: Extension functions in C++/PHP
article.p: This section provides a guide for the memory management of the SaxonC C++ API.

The SaxonC API documentation is a good place to start as each method has relevant information about the input arguments and output from each of the methods. Some of these methods return pointers which require deallocation of the memory. For many otf these the responsibility is on the caller. For example, the SaxonProcessor parse functions (parseXmlFromString, parseXmlFromFile) returns a pointer to the created XdmNode object on the heap memory. The caller must deallocate the memory used by calling delete otherwise memory will be leaked. The same can be said for the pointer to the XdmValue object returned by the methods evaluate and evaluateSingle in the XPathProcessor class. This is the same for the XdmValue object pointers returned by methods in the XsltExecutable and in XQueryProcessor.

The XdmNode object is as a tree structure. As you navigate the tree the child object pointers are created lazily. Therefore, when these methods are called: getChildren(), axisNodes, getChild and getAttributeNodes you will get one or more XdmNode objects created as pointers. The caller is responsible for deallocation of the memory using delete. It is important to note that calling these methods from the same node object repeatedly creates the child nodes again. The is no caching.

For the XdmValue the XdmItem objects it contains cached. When you retrieve an XdmItem * using itemAt or getHead the caller is responsible for deallocating memory of the pointer to XdmItem(s). Notice in the above example that pointers item0_1 and item0_2 point to the same object. Therefore, we should only call delete on one of the pointers.

For the retrieval of string values in SaxonC C++ in the API we allocate the char pointer array using operator new. This is because the string allocation on the heap is created from the Java code. The callers to the API methods must deallocate the memory usedwe use operator delete on the pointer char array.
The exception to this are the methods SaxonProcessor.version(). These methods create string on the stack therefore memory management is internally handled.
